answer: A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 109 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The bridge detector writes to inlet, and sable shows every merge. Submissions that land within 293 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 33 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
